subject: Art & Design
title: Alignment: Left, Right, Center, and Justified
description: A quick win: understand Alignment: Left, Right, Center, and Justified.

hook.text: Centered text on a wedding invitation looks elegant. Centered text in a long article looks amateurish.

buildup.text: Left-aligned (ragged right) is the default for Western body text. The uneven right edge aids reading flow.

discovery.text: Justified text (even on both sides) looks clean but creates uneven word spacing — 'rivers' of white space.

twist.text: Justified text only works well with hyphenation. Without it, spacing problems are unavoidable.

climax.text: Right-aligned text is rare in body copy but works for pull quotes, captions, and accents.

punchline.text: Left-align by default. Break the rule only with good reason.

quiz.question: What problem does justified text often create?
options: Uneven word spacing that creates 'rivers' of white space
Letters that are too small to read

details.summary: Text alignment — left-aligned (ragged right), right-aligned, centered, or justified (even edges) — affects readability and aesthetic feel. Left-aligned is most readable for Western languages. Centered suits formal headings.
details.whyItMatters: Alignment is among the first typographic choices and affects everything that follows. Left-aligned text is the safest default for readability, while justified and centered alignment serve specific aesthetic and formal purposes.
takeaways: Left-aligned text is most readable for Western languages
Centered alignment suits headings and formal compositions
Justified text creates clean edges but risks uneven spacing

faq.question: Why does justified text sometimes look bad?
faq.answer: Justified text stretches word spacing to create even edges. In narrow columns, this creates wide, uneven gaps between words — 'rivers of white' flowing down the text block. Professional typesetting uses hyphenation and tracking to minimize rivers, but web justification often lacks these refinements.

faq.question: When should you use right-aligned text?
faq.answer: Right-aligned text is common in right-to-left languages (Arabic, Hebrew) and for specific design purposes: numbers in tables (aligning decimal points), captions beside images, pull quotes, and certain formal or invitation designs. For body text in English, it reduces readability significantly.
